body:
Ibrahim Khan: Kicking off parity decisions for streaming examples across Python/TS/Go + docs. Need to lock (a) event naming shown in samples, (b) how we assemble the final message, (c) tool-call streaming + partial args handling. Please reply w/ blockers by EOD so we can unblock ENG-4821.

Ibrahim Khan: Linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/audit-streaming-examples-across-sdks

Monica Patel: +1. Let’s make sure we don’t invent new protocol in examples. Show what actually comes across the wire + what SDK exposes today.

Dana Lo: For TS: current example uses `event.type` values like `response.output_text.delta` (from older snippet). I can align to whatever we decide, but we should pick names that map 1:1 to the SDK stream objects.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go stream is currently just “chunk structs” and a helper builds up final. I’m fine changing the printed labels in docs, but we should be clear what’s “example labels” vs actual payload fields.

Elliot Price: From docs perspective we need consistent headings / pseudo-event taxonomy across tabs. We can say “Event: message.delta” etc even if underlying is `type: response.output_text.delta` as long as we show the real `type` in code.

Brian Murphy: Strong preference: examples should switch on the actual `type` string in the stream event. If we want “friendly names”, keep it in comments only.

Sabrina James: +1 to switching on actual `type`. Support sees copy/paste snippets; any mismatch causes tickets.

Wei Chen: Agree. Also please call out that streaming tool-call args can arrive fragmented (SUP-18421). That’s the top confusion in Hosted API docs.

Ibrahim Khan: Proposal for canonical sample structure:
1) Iterate stream events.
2) Maintain 3 accumulators: `assistant_text`, `tool_calls` (by id), and `final_response` (optional object).
3) Print deltas inline (optional), but assemble final deterministically.
4) On `response.completed` (or final event), validate/return.

Ibrahim Khan: Event names to show in code (actual):
- `response.started`
- `response.output_text.delta`
- `response.output_text.completed`
- `response.tool_call.delta` (args partial)
- `response.tool_call.completed` (args complete)
- `response.completed`
- `response.failed`

Dana Lo: TS SDK today emits `response.output_text.delta` + `response.completed` etc. Tool calls: I think we have `response.tool_call.delta` already from the compat layer. Need to double-check.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go SDK: tool call stream events exist but naming is slightly different (`tool_call.delta` without `response.` prefix) in older fixture. I can shim in example code, but that’s exactly the parity problem.

Brian Murphy: Let’s not add shims. If Go is different, either (a) update Go SDK event type strings, or (b) in docs tab for Go, show the Go-specific ones (but then docs aren’t “parity”).

Monica Patel: We should converge SDKs to the same `type` names if feasible. If it’s just example-level wrappers, ok, but I’d rather fix Go/TS than fork docs.

Sahana Iyer: If we’re changing event types, golden tests will catch this. But we need to decide soon so we don’t churn fixtures across repos.

Ibrahim Khan: Re Go: Mateusz, can you confirm actual event type strings from current released version? Not what’s in the old README.

Mateusz Zielinski: Checking now. I’ll paste from running `examples/streaming/main.go` against staging.

GitHub Bot: Mateusz Zielinski opened PR #744 in redwood-sdk-go: "streaming consumer loop update" https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-go/pull/744

Mateusz Zielinski: From PR #744 branch output, event types are:
- `response.started`
- `response.output_text.delta`
- `response.tool_call.delta`
- `response.completed`
So we’re mostly aligned already; older docs were wrong.

Dana Lo: Nice. TS has all those too. For tool calls we also see `response.tool_call.completed` in some models, but not always; sometimes only `delta` then final snapshot on `response.completed`.

Brian Murphy: That’s important nuance. Examples should not assume `tool_call.completed` always appears. Safer rule: always merge deltas; final authoritative state is whatever `response.completed` contains.

Wei Chen: +1. Docs should say: “you may or may not receive *completed* markers depending on model/provider; always handle partial deltas + finalize on completed response.”

Sabrina James: For printing, I suggest we only print tool calls when we have a parseable args JSON (or when response completes). Otherwise people think args are “truncated”.

Ibrahim Khan: So example algorithm for tool args:
- Keep `tool_calls[id].arguments_json += delta_fragment`
- Don’t `json.loads` until either:
  a) we receive `response.tool_call.completed`, OR
  b) we reach `response.completed`
- If parsing fails at completion, retry once with “please re-emit valid JSON args” guidance (or log + surface error)

Monica Patel: Retry behavior in examples should be conservative. Maybe show “validate + if invalid, re-ask model to call tool again” rather than doing hidden retries.

Elliot Price: For docs: we can include a “Known pitfalls” callout section and keep code minimal. But sample should show the pattern clearly.

Dana Lo: What about naming: `tool_call` vs `tool_calls`? TS uses `tool_calls` array in the final message. Streaming events are singular `tool_call.delta`.

Brian Murphy: In code: use `toolCallsByID` (map) for assembly; final model output likely has an array. We can show both.

Ibrahim Khan: Decision check (please react):
A) Switch on actual `event.type` strings (`response.output_text.delta`, etc)
B) Accumulate tool args as strings; parse only when complete
C) Final assembly happens on `response.completed` (authoritative)

Monica Patel: (reaction: :thumbsup:) A/B/C

Dana Lo: (reaction: :thumbsup:) A/B/C

Mateusz Zielinski: (reaction: :thumbsup:) A/B/C

Wei Chen: (reaction: :thumbsup:) A/B/C

Brian Murphy: (reaction: :thumbsup:) A/B/C

Sahana Iyer: (reaction: :thumbsup:) A/B/C (also helps golden tests)

Ibrahim Khan: Great. Next: sample structure consistent across languages. Suggested sections:
1) Define tools (name, description, JSON schema)
2) Send request w/ `stream: true`
3) Stream loop: handle text deltas + tool deltas
4) If tool call requested: execute tool(s) (support parallel)
5) Send tool result message(s)
6) Continue until final assistant message

Sabrina James: +1 and please keep same comments across languages (so docs tabs don’t drift). Like “// 1) Define tool schema” etc.

Dana Lo: Parallel tool calls: TS example can `await Promise.all(toolCalls.map(runTool))`. But should we show parallel by default? Might confuse beginners.

Wei Chen: We should show parallel but with a one-line note: “If tools are independent, run in parallel.” Lots of agent users expect that.

Brian Murphy: As long as we make it explicit that tool execution is on the client side and you must pass results back as tool-result messages.

Ibrahim Khan: Re links/PRs:
- Python example refresh: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-python/pull/2874
- TS types + examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-typescript/pull/1932
- Go stream loop: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-go/pull/744
Docs PR will follow once we freeze this thread.

Linear Bot: ENG-4822 created by Ibrahim Khan: "add golden tests for streaming tool calls" https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4822/add-golden-tests-for-streaming-tool-calls

Sahana Iyer: For ENG-4822, we need to agree fixture format: store raw stream events (JSON lines) + expected assembled output. If event types are stable, tests will be less flaky.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go side: I’ll make fixtures match raw event JSON. We can share a common fixture set across repos? Or at least identical transcripts.

Monica Patel: Common fixture set is ideal but logistics are tough. Minimum: keep the transcript semantics identical and document any provider-specific differences.

Elliot Price: Docs can link to “runnable examples repo” instead of embedding giant tool-loop code. But we still need short snippets in docs.

Ibrahim Khan: Action items:
- Dana: confirm TS tool-call event coverage + update sample to parse tool args only at completion.
- Mateusz: land PR #744 and verify tool delta behavior w/ at least 2 models.
- Sabrina: review Python PR #2874 for the same algorithm; make sure printing doesn’t imply args are truncated.
- Elliot/Wei: once code is final, we’ll update docs tabs to match.

Dana Lo: Ack. I’ll add a tiny helper `appendToolArgsDelta(id, delta)` in TS example to make it obvious.

Mateusz Zielinski: Ack. PR #744 already includes helper `AssembleResponse()`; I’ll ensure it handles tool args fragments.

Sabrina James: I’ll review Python PR and add a “don’t parse incremental JSON” comment.

Wei Chen: I’ll draft the doc pitfall copy: “partial tool args are normal; finalize on response.completed” + link SUP-18421 workaround.

Connor O'Brien: Heads up for releases: if event type strings are unchanged, we can ship examples without bumping major versions. Please flag me if any SDK behavior changes.

Ibrahim Khan: No behavior change planned; this is mostly example + docs alignment. If Go/TS need any public type tweaks, we’ll route through Monica.

Brian Murphy: One more nit: make sure examples handle `response.failed` and show how to surface the error message cleanly.

Dana Lo: Yup, TS sample can `throw new Error(event.error?.message ?? 'stream failed')`.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go sample will return `fmt.Errorf("stream failed: %s", errMsg)` and stop consuming.

Ibrahim Khan: Cool. I’ll summarize this in the parity conventions doc + link back here in ENG-4821. (reaction: :white_check_mark:)
